question: A magnet is pushed towards a closed conducting coil. The coil opposes the motion of the magnet. Explain why this opposition is produced and what happens to the mechanical work done.

options.A:
The approaching magnet changes the flux through the coil and induces a current whose magnetic effect opposes the approach, according to Lenz's law.
The mechanical work done by the external agent is converted into electrical energy and finally heat in the coil.
options.B:
The coil opposes the magnet because it becomes permanently magnetised.
The mechanical work is destroyed when the magnet reaches the coil.
options.C:
The coil assists the approaching magnet because induced current always increases the change in flux.
The mechanical work is converted entirely into gravitational potential energy.
options.D:
No induced current is produced because the coil is closed.
No energy transformation occurs.
